title: DSWD supports CWC's call vs. sexualized humor involving children
summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development on Saturday said it fully supports the Council for the Welfare of Children, its attached agency, in calling out the use of sexualized humor involving…

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Saturday said it fully supports the Council for the Welfare of Children (CWC), its attached agency, in calling out the use of sexualized humor involving children in comedy sets and online content.
In a statement, the DSWD pointed out a recent remark by comedian JP Aguilera of Pencilbox Comedy, who utilized playgrounds and their connection with children as a sexual reference.

“The DSWD stands firmly behind the CWC in reminding performers and content creators, and of course everyone, that children must never be reduced to punchlines or subjects of sexual insinuations,” said DSWD spokesperson Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao.
Dumlao said that while creative expression is valued, jokes that downplay the vulnerability of minors risk normalizing inappropriate behavior toward them.

The DSWD cited Section 4 (n) of Republic Act (RA) No. 11930, or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act, that strictly prohibits sexualizing children by presenting minors as objects of sexual fantasy or making children conversational subjects of sexual fantasies on any online or digital platform.
According to the agency, violators found guilty under the law face the penalty of reclusion temporal in its maximum period and a fine ranging from P800,000 to P1 million.

“Hindi dapat ginagawang biro ang dignidad at kaligtasan ng mga bata dahil responsibilidad ng lahat na protektahan ang mga kabataan laban sa anumang uri ng pang-aabuso at pagsasamantala, lalo na sa social media at iba pang digital platforms,” Dumlao said.

(The dignity and safety of children should not be made a joke because it is everyone's responsibility to protect young people against any form of abuse and exploitation, especially on social media and other digital platforms.)

The DSWD as well restated the call of CWC Executive Director Undersecretary Angelo Tapales for entertainers, media practitioners, and digital content creators to observe the CWC Guide for Media Practitioners in the Reporting and Coverage of Children to ensure the privacy, dignity, and best interests of minors are respected at all times.

“Nananawagan ang DSWD sa mga nasa entertainment industry at content creation na maging responsable sa bawat materyal na inilalabas sa publiko dahil malaki ang epekto ng mga salita sa kung paano tinatrato ng lipunan ang mga bata,” Dumlao said.
(DSWD calls on those in the entertainment industry and content creation to be responsible for every material released to the public because words have a great impact on how society treats children.)

GMA News Online contacted Pencilbox Comedy to get its comments and will update this story once it issues a statement. Efforts so far made to reach out to Aguilera have been unsuccessful as of posting time. —KG, GMA News
